Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# Pull Request Information

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 26
- **Additions**: +3155
- **Deletions**: -31
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T04:29:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1776._

> ℹ️ **16 resolved thread(s) excluded; 8 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 17 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1046

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 Formatting drift — `dart format` is not clean on 4 touched files

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` (Dart 3.13.5) reports changes in:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` (2 missing blank lines, e.g. after the `sessions` getter at line 936)
- `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` (the `applicationNote` `'sessions'` arm needs a wrapped string)
- `test/session_retention_config_test.dart`
- `test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart`

`origin/main`'s version of `cli_config.dart` is format-clean under the same SDK, so this PR introduced the drift. The pre-commit hook self-heals staged files and CI does not gate on format, so nothing breaks — but the next commit from any author with the hook will reformat these lines, adding noise to a future diff.

Suggested: run `dart format lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart lib/src/config/config_service.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart` before merge.

---

### Thread 18 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 501

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. The doc comment scopes null to tests, and today every production boot path wires a real store (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` for the CLI; the clean verb passes one too) — so this is hardening, not a bug.

But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

Suggested: in `enforceAtBoot()`, treat `presenceStore == null` the same as a failed probe (abort with a note), or add an explicit `allowMissingPresence` flag so the test convenience is opt-in rather than the default shape.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

## Fixed — parity gate classified

`sessions` is now classified in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` → `fileOnlyConfigKeys`, with the WHY matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->` intent:

```dart
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Verification: `dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` → 13/13 green (both previously-red tests — "every parsed yaml key is classified" and "the audit table covers every key exactly once" — pass; `sessions` is single-owner, in no `SharedSetting.yamlKeys`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6vC56s` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:501`)

💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. The doc comment scopes null to tests, and today every production boot path wires a real store (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` for the CLI; the clean verb passes one too) — so this is hardening, not a bug.

But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

Suggested: in `enforceAtBoot()`, treat `presenceStore == null` the same as a failed probe (abort with a note), or add an explicit `allowMissingPresence` flag so the test convenience is opt-in rather than the default shape.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —

   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. ## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1776._

> ℹ️ **16 resolved thread(s) excluded; 8 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 17 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1046

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 Formatting drift — `dart format` is not clean on 4 touched files

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` (Dart 3.13.5) reports changes in:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` (2 missing blank lines, e.g. after the `sessions` getter at line 936)
- `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` (the `applicationNote` `'sessions'` arm needs a wrapped string)
- `test/session_retention_config_test.dart`
- `test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart`

`origin/main`'s version of `cli_config.dart` is format-clean under the same SDK, so this PR introduced the drift. The pre-commit hook self-heals staged files and CI does not gate on format, so nothing breaks — but the next commit from any author with the hook will reformat these lines, adding noise to a future diff.

Suggested: run `dart format lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart lib/src/config/config_service.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart` before merge.

---

### Thread 18 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 501

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. The doc comment scopes null to tests, and today every production boot path wires a real store (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` for the CLI; the clean verb passes one too) — so this is hardening, not a bug.

But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

Suggested: in `enforceAtBoot()`, treat `presenceStore == null` the same as a failed probe (abort with a note), or add an explicit `allowMissingPresence` flag so the test convenience is opt-in rather than the default shape.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

## Fixed — parity gate classified

`sessions` is now classified in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` → `fileOnlyConfigKeys`, with the WHY matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->` intent:

```dart
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Verification: `dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` → 13/13 green (both previously-red tests — "every parsed yaml key is classified" and "the audit table covers every key exactly once" — pass; `sessions` is single-owner, in no `SharedSetting.yamlKeys`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

# pr-1776: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve

the unused surface.

overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a

least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

Let me start by understanding the task. I'm a rework agent for one PR. I need to:
1. Read all input files in the ticket folder
2. Answer every open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json
3. Apply code/test fixes following TDD
4. Push

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 26
- **Additions**: +3155
- **Deletions**: -31
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T04:29:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1776._

> ℹ️ **16 resolved thread(s) excluded; 8 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 17 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1046

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 Formatting drift — `dart format` is not clean on 4 touched files

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` (Dart 3.13.5) reports changes in:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` (2 missing blank lines, e.g. after the `sessions` getter at line 936)
- `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` (the `applicationNote` `'sessions'` arm needs a wrapped string)
- `test/session_retention_config_test.dart`
- `test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart`

`origin/main`'s version of `cli_config.dart` is format-clean under the same SDK, so this PR introduced the drift. The pre-commit hook self-heals staged files and CI does not gate on format, so nothing breaks — but the next commit from any author with the hook will reformat these lines, adding noise to a future diff.

Suggested: run `dart format lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart lib/src/config/config_service.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart` before merge.

---

### Thread 18 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 501

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. The doc comment scopes null to tests, and today every production boot path wires a real store (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` for the CLI; the clean verb passes one too) — so this is hardening, not a bug.

But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

Suggested: in `enforceAtBoot()`, treat `presenceStore == null` the same as a failed probe (abort with a note), or add an explicit `allowMissingPresence` flag so the test convenience is opt-in rather than the default shape.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

## Fixed — parity gate classified

`sessions` is now classified in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` → `fileOnlyConfigKeys`, with the WHY matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->` intent:

```dart
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Verification: `dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` → 13/13 green (both previously-red tests — "every parsed yaml key is classified" and "the audit table covers every key exactly once" — pass; `sessions` is single-owner, in no `SharedSetting.yamlKeys`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 26
- **Additions**: +3155
- **Deletions**: -31
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T04:29:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1776._

> ℹ️ **16 resolved thread(s) excluded; 8 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 17 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1046

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 Formatting drift — `dart format` is not clean on 4 touched files

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` (Dart 3.13.5) reports changes in:

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` (2 missing blank lines, e.g. after the `sessions` getter at line 936)
- `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` (the `applicationNote` `'sessions'` arm needs a wrapped string)
- `test/session_retention_config_test.dart`
- `test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart`

`origin/main`'s version of `cli_config.dart` is format-clean under the same SDK, so this PR introduced the drift. The pre-commit hook self-heals staged files and CI does not gate on format, so nothing breaks — but the next commit from any author with the hook will reformat these lines, adding noise to a future diff.

Suggested: run `dart format lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart lib/src/config/config_service.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart` before merge.

---

### Thread 18 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 501

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. The doc comment scopes null to tests, and today every production boot path wires a real store (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` for the CLI; the clean verb passes one too) — so this is hardening, not a bug.

But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

Suggested: in `enforceAtBoot()`, treat `presenceStore == null` the same as a failed probe (abort with a note), or add an explicit `allowMissingPresence` flag so the test convenience is opt-in rather than the default shape.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

## Fixed — parity gate classified

`sessions` is now classified in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` → `fileOnlyConfigKeys`, with the WHY matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->` intent:

```dart
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Verification: `dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` → 13/13 green (both previously-red tests — "every parsed yaml key is classified" and "the audit table covers every key exactly once" — pass; `sessions` is single-owner, in no `SharedSetting.yamlKeys`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_Termi…
